newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers retiring state workers up to $10,300.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers retiring state workers up to $10,300.

text.p: The Egyptian state is offering employees in unprofitable state companies lump-sum compensation of between 12,000 pounds and 35,000 pounds ($3,530 and $10,300) if they accept early voluntary retirement, Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri told parliament on Sunday.
The aim is to cut staffing levels at the companies and increase profitability in readiness for possible privatisation.
Male employees aged between 50 and 58 and female employees between 45 and 58 are eligible for the scheme, Ganzouri said. They must have worked for at least 20 years, he added.
Ganzouri said the government expected about 20,000 workers to take advantage of the scheme.

The lump sum of 12,000 pounds applies to employees of grade 6 who retire between the ages of 54 and 58, the 35,000 pounds applies to grade 1 employees who retire between the ages of 50 and 52, government papers said. Retirement age in Egypt is 60.
The papers did not give details of compensation for women employees who retire before the age of 50.
The government has said the early retirment scheme could cost it up to 11 billion pounds.

Earlier this month a senior official in the ministry responsible for privatisation said the state had already spent 200 million pounds on 11,000 public-sector workers who opted for early retirement -- an average of about 18,000 pounds each.

The official, Public Enterprise Ministry undersecretary Mukhtar Khattab, said overstaffing levels stood at around 18 percent in the public-enterprise sector, which now employs 908,000 people. Potential investors might estimate the overstaffing level at between 35 to 40 percent, he added.
The public-enterprise sector includes more than 300 state companies slated for eventual privatisation. It does not include utilities, public transport, banking and many other sectors.
